title: Invariant Structure Learning with Pre-trained Language Models for Spatio-temporal Graph

problem.claim: PLM deployment in critical spatiotemporal forecasting systems is vulnerable to brittleness under distribution shifts.

gap.claim: Existing PLM-based approaches primarily learn statistical correlations and may fail to distinguish stable mechanisms from spurious environmental features.

contributions.claim: InvSTG-PLM is an invariance-aware spatiotemporal graph learning framework that grounds PLMs in invariant structures.
The framework formalizes invariance through token re-assignment and uses a variance-regularized objective to penalize reliance on variant factors.
InvSTG-Tokenizer and InvSTG-Adapter separate invariant structure from variant factors and align invariant geometric structures with PLM semantic space.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Theoretical analysis reports a deterministic robustness bound in which mean–variance control upper bounds worst-case risk over simulated environments.
Experiments on multiple benchmarks report that InvSTG-PLM outperforms existing methods and shows improved robustness under distribution shifts.

narrative_sequence.summary: PLM-based spatiotemporal forecasting is brittle under distribution shifts in critical systems.
Prior approaches can conflate stable graph mechanisms with spurious environmental features.
The paper proposes InvSTG-PLM to ground PLMs in invariant structures.
Token re-assignment, variance regularization, and specialized tokenizer and adapter components implement the invariance principle.
The abstract reports a robustness bound and improved benchmark performance and shift robustness.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates invariant structure from variant factors before aligning representations with PLM semantic space.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly modeling stable and changing factors may improve robustness when deployment environments differ from training environments.

application.claim: For other structured forecasting tasks, consider representation-level environment simulation and objectives that penalize dependence on variant factors.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach helps when relevant factors are not separable into invariant and variant components.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, distribution-shift settings, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe computational costs, implementation details, or failure cases.
